# Japanese Grimoire · japanesegrimoire.com

> English-language site by Dr. Mark Hosak about the real Japanese traditions behind the hand signs, spirits and sacred places known from anime and manga: Kuji Kiri and mudras, yokai and kami, onmyodo, Shugendo, Shingon (esoteric Buddhism), Shinto, and the sacred places of Japan. Articles give history, background and meaning; practice happens in the Japanese Grimoire Society community and in live events. Not affiliated with any anime series.

## About the author
- Dr. Mark Hosak: Japanologist (PhD, Heidelberg University), about three years of research at Kyoto University on Buddhist art, architecture and ritual; Shingon practitioner and researcher; successor of Taguchi Sensei in his line of Ninjutsu; walked all 88 temples of the Shikoku pilgrimage; author of books on Reiki and its Japanese roots; founder of Shingon Reiki (https://www.shingon-reiki.com/en).

## Kuji Kiri & Hand Seals
- [Kuji Kiri & Japanese Hand Seals · Real Meaning and History](https://japanesegrimoire.com/kuji-kiri): Kuji Kiri, Kuji-in and the mudras of esoteric Buddhism: where the nine seals come from, what they mean, and how they ended up in Naruto and Jujutsu Kaisen. By Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Kuji Kiri: The Nine Hand Seals and Where They Really Come From](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/kuji-kiri-nine-hand-seals): Kuji Kiri and Kuji-in explained by a Japanologist: the nine characters 臨兵闘者皆陣列在前, their Chinese origins, how Japan turned them into its own system, and where the nine seals still live today.
- [Mudras in Japanese Esoteric Buddhism: The Hand Seals Behind Kuji-in](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/mudras-japanese-esoteric-buddhism): What mudras mean in Japanese esoteric Buddhism (mikkyō): the 'in' or hand seal, the five elements in the fingers, how to read the hands of buddha statues in Nara, Kamakura and Kyoto, and how the mudras connect to Kuji-in. By Dr. Mark Hosak.

## Anime → Real Japan
- [Anime → Real Japan · The Traditions Behind Naruto, JJK and Demon Slayer](https://japanesegrimoire.com/anime-real-japan): Naruto's hand signs, Jujutsu Kaisen's domain expansions, Demon Slayer's Hinokami Kagura: Japanologist Dr. Mark Hosak traces what anime borrowed from real Japanese religion and folklore.
- [Are Naruto Hand Signs Real? The Kuji-in Behind the Jutsu](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/naruto-hand-signs-real-kuji-in): Naruto's twelve hand signs are named after the Chinese zodiac. The real Japanese tradition has nine seals, the Kuji-in. A Japanologist explains what's invented, what's real, and the Edo-period legend hiding in the cast.
- [Jujutsu Kaisen's Domain Expansion Hand Signs and the Real Mudras Behind Them](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/jujutsu-kaisen-domain-expansion-hand-signs): Gojo, Sukuna, Megumi and Jogo: fans link the Domain Expansion hand signs in Jujutsu Kaisen to real mudras of Japanese esoteric Buddhism. A Japanologist explains Taishakuten, Enmaten, the Medicine Buddha and the real Ryōmen Sukuna.
- [Demon Slayer's Real Japan: Hinokami Kagura, Hanafuda Earrings and Oni Lore](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/demon-slayer-real-japan): The real Japan behind Demon Slayer: kagura dances for the kami, the hearth kami behind the name Kamado, hanafuda cards, why oni have horns and tiger-skin loincloths, and the real sword that is said to have cut a demon. By Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Amaterasu and Susanoo: The Real Kami Behind Naruto's Most Famous Jutsu](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/amaterasu-susanoo-real-kami): The real Amaterasu, Tsukuyomi and Susanoo from the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki: the birth of the three kami, the sun hiding in the rock cave, Susanoo and the eight-headed serpent, the sword Kusanagi, and the Totsuka sword and Yata mirror in Naruto. By Dr. Mark Hosak.

## Yokai & Kami
- [Yokai & Kami · An Encyclopedia of Japanese Spirits](https://japanesegrimoire.com/yokai-kami): Kitsune, tengu, oni, kappa and the kami of Japan: where they come from, how Japan depicts them, and where you can still meet them today. By Japanologist Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [The Nine-Tailed Fox: Kitsune in Japanese Folklore and the Inari Faith](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/nine-tailed-fox-kitsune): Kyūbi no kitsune, the nine-tailed fox: its Chinese origins, the legend of Tamamo-no-Mae and the Killing Stone of Nasu, and why the foxes at Inari shrines are messengers, not gods. By Japanologist Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Tengu: Mountain Spirits, Yamabushi and the Masters of Mount Kurama](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/tengu-mountain-spirits): Tengu explained by a Japanologist: from the 'heavenly dog' of the Nihon Shoki to the crow tengu and the long-nosed daitengu, Sōjōbō of Mount Kurama, the young Yoshitsune, and why tengu dress like yamabushi.
- [Yokai List: 24 Japanese Spirits and What They Really Mean](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/yokai-list-japanese-spirits): A Japanologist's yokai list: kitsune, tanuki, kappa, tengu, oni, yuki-onna, rokurokubi, tsukumogami and more. Where each Japanese spirit comes from, what it meant, and where you can still find it today.
- [Oni: Japan's Demons from Folklore to Setsubun](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/oni-japanese-demons): Oni explained by a Japanologist: the 'hidden ones' of early Japan, the demon gate, Shuten-dōji and Ibaraki-dōji, the oni of Momotarō and Kibitsu Shrine, Hannya masks, Namahage, and the temple that shouts 'demons in' at Setsubun.
- [Japanese Mythology: A Beginner's Map of Gods, Spirits and Sacred Stories](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/japanese-mythology-beginners-map): A beginner's guide to Japanese mythology: the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, Izanagi and Izanami, Amaterasu and Susanoo, the Izumo myths and the white hare, the descent of Ninigi, the eight million kami, and how kami and buddhas came together. By Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Japanese Ghost Stories and Urban Legends, and What They Reveal](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/japanese-ghost-stories-urban-legends): Yūrei, kaidan and urban legends of Japan: why Japanese ghosts wear white and have no feet, the great classic ghost stories of Oiwa, Okiku and the Peony Lantern, vengeful spirits who became kami, and modern legends from Kuchisake-onna to Kisaragi Station.

## Esoteric Japan
- [Esoteric Japan · Shingon, Shugendō, Onmyōdō and Shinto Magic](https://japanesegrimoire.com/esoteric-japan): Esoteric Buddhism (Shingon), Shugendō, onmyōdō and Shinto: Japan's magical and spiritual traditions explained by Dr. Mark Hosak, Japanologist and Shingon practitioner and researcher.
- [Onmyōdō and Abe no Seimei: Japan's Real Yin-Yang Masters](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/onmyodo-abe-no-seimei): What onmyōdō really was: the yin-yang bureau of the Heian court, the historical Abe no Seimei (921–1005), shikigami, the pentagram of Seimei Shrine, and the fox mother Kuzunoha. By Japanologist Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Omamori: How Japanese Amulets Work and How to Treat Them](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/omamori-japanese-amulets): What an omamori is, what's inside the pouch, the different kinds (traffic safety, exams, love, protection), the birth-year buddhas of Shingon temples, and how to treat and return an omamori. By Japanologist Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Ofuda and Japanese Talismans: Paper Protection from Shrines and Temples](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/ofuda-japanese-talismans): What ofuda are, how Japanese paper talismans developed from Daoist charms, the crow talismans of Kumano, the Sominsōrai and Tsuno Daishi charms, and how ofuda are kept and returned. By Japanologist Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Misogi: The Real Shinto Purification Behind the "Misogi Challenge"](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/misogi-shinto-purification): What misogi really is: the myth of Izanagi's purification, kegare and harae, misogi under waterfalls and in the sea, the everyday version at every shrine, and how the 'misogi challenge' borrowed the word. By Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Shugendō and the Yamabushi: Japan's Mountain Mystics](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/shugendo-yamabushi): Shugendō explained by a Japanologist and practitioner: En no Gyōja, the mountains as living mandalas, the yamabushi's clothing and tools, Ōmine, Kumano and Dewa Sanzan, the Meiji ban, and Shugendō's link to Kuji Kiri. By Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Shingon Buddhism and Kūkai: Japan's Esoteric Path in Plain English](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/shingon-buddhism-kukai): Shingon Buddhism explained by a Japanologist and Shingon practitioner and researcher: the life of Kūkai (Kōbō Daishi), the 'true word,' Dainichi Nyorai and the two mandalas, the three mysteries, Kōyasan and Tō-ji, and the Shikoku pilgrimage. By Dr. Mark Hosak.

## Sacred Places
- [Sacred Places of Japan · Shrines, Temples and Mountains of Power](https://japanesegrimoire.com/sacred-places): Fushimi Inari, Mount Kurama, the Kumano Kodo and the torii gates of Japan, seen as sacred places rather than tourist spots. By Dr. Mark Hosak, who walked all 88 temples of Shikoku.
- [Fushimi Inari: The Spiritual Meaning Behind 10,000 Torii](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/fushimi-inari-torii-meaning): Fushimi Inari Taisha beyond the travel guide: the founding legend of 711, why there are about 10,000 torii and who donates them, the fox messengers, the stone mounds on Mount Inari and the shrine's link to Kūkai's Tō-ji. By Dr. Mark Hosak.
- [Mount Kurama: Tengu, Sōjōbō and the Mountain Behind Reiki](https://japanesegrimoire.com/blog/mount-kurama-tengu-reiki): Mount Kurama north of Kyoto: why it's really a range, the founding visions of Kurama-dera, the three spirits Senju Kannon, Bishamonten and Maōson, Sōjōbō and Yoshitsune, Mikao Usui's 21 days on the mountain, and the Kurama Fire Festival. By Dr. Mark Hosak.
